en: The Philippine eagle is the national bird and is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
Sampaguita, a white jasmine flower, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the Constitution.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed an improvised bamboo incubator to provide medical care for rural Filipino babies.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-step forward, one-step backward dance.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines, alongside over 150 regional languages.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses.
Every Filipino citizen who is at least eighteen years old has the right to vote in elections.
Bayanihan refers to the traditional Filipino practice of community members helping a family move their nipa hut.
Narra, a hard wood from the pterocarpus indicus tree, is the official national tree of the Philippines.
